Dylan / Irene —

Attaching the artifacts I pulled together. Highlights below for the vendor packet (one-paragraph bullets we can paste into the RFI):

1) Isolation model (short):
- Logical tenant isolation is enforced at three layers: orchestration (per-tenant scheduling pools), process boundary (one inference worker per tenant namespace), and network (sidecar per-tenant egress/filtering). We run a lightweight sidecar that handles per-request provenance headers and enforces outbound ACLs.
- Control plane endpoints (model repository, scheduler, control API) are on a dedicated management network segment and never traverse tenant egress paths.

2) Egress controls & evidence:
- Outbound traffic exits via a tenant-tagged NAT gateway that applies per-tenant ACLs. We produce an ACL matrix that maps tenant IDs to allowed destinations; this is exported as CSV.
- Audit log copies: runtime logs are recorded locally then streamed to REDWOOD-AUDIT (write-once) S3 buckets per customer; the same events are hashed and an event digest posted to a signing service (HSM-backed) every 10 minutes. The digest file and per-minute signed envelope are included in the audit_provenance_digest.txt.

3) Network diagram:
- See tenant_boundary_network_diagram_v1.svg — it annotates: tenant ingress (TLS terminated at edge), per-tenant inference pool, sidecar proxies, KV cache boundaries, control plane in separate VCN, and egress NAT clusters.

4) Quick mitigations list for the one-pager:
- mTLS for all internal RPCs, microsegmentation by tenant, KV-cache access tokens that are single-use and short TTL, seccomp + namespace isolation on worker containers, periodic cryptographic hash of log batches, and integrated alerting for anomalous egress.

Attachments I uploaded to the drive folder and included locally: tenant_boundary_network_diagram_v1.svg (SVG), egress_acl_matrix_v2026-07-09.csv (CSV), audit_provenance_digest.txt (TXT). Also added a README with usage notes.

Let me know if you want the diagram annotated with attacker paths — I can add that and produce a PDF.

- Vanessa

Redwood Inference

Adding the threat-model summary and a small note on provenance validation steps. Draft below for the one-page: 

Threat model summary (top hypotheses):
- Supply chain compromise (model artifact tampering): mitigated by signed model manifests, provenance checksums, and immutable model-store references.
- Lateral movement from compromised tenant workload: mitigations include strong microsegmentation, sidecar-enforced RBAC, kernel isolations (seccomp, namespaces) and ephemeral creds.
- KV-cache poisoning / prefix-inference: mitigations include per-tenant cache namespaces, request fingerprinting, and rate-limited KV policies.
- Egress exfiltration via allowed destinations: mitigations include per-tenant allowlists, egress DLP hooks, and real-time flow logs routed to customer audit buckets.
- Control plane impersonation: mitigations include mutually authenticated control plane certs, key rotation, and independent control-plane logging.

Provenance validation steps (what Orchid can do):
1) Pull the per-company S3 audit bundle and compare event sequence hashes to our signed digest file.
2) Verify HSM signature on the digest (we will provide the public verification cert).
3) Validate egress ACL mapping in the CSV against observed flow logs for a chosen 24h window (we can export a sample window if they need it).

I also annotated the diagram with three attack-path overlays (supply-chain, lateral-movement, egress-exfil) and uploaded a PDF named threat_model_summary_2026-07-09.pdf to the same Drive folder.

- Irene
Principal Security Architect
Redwood Inference
